Veloxa CXO Cockpit: Candidate Brief
The ask
A note from Ananya Rao, CEO of Veloxa Technologies (a 180-person B2B SaaS company in Bengaluru):
I run this company mostly on gut and on whoever reaches my inbox first. I want one place where I can ask a question about the company and get a straight answer: what each team is actually doing, where we are stuck, and what I should worry about. I don't want another dashboard nobody opens.
Build it on a version of Veloxa I can test: start with 14 people across engineering, finance, HR and marketing, and make them feel like real colleagues with real lives, not spreadsheet rows. IT will hand you exports from our systems; they're the best record we have, but they're not clean.
I won't have time to meet you. My assistant recorded a few of my calls with the leadership team; you'll get the auto-generated summaries as they come in. The transcription tool isn't great, and my team doesn't always agree with each other or with me. You have 10 working days.
What you get, and what you don't
You will not meet the CEO or any leader. You learn about Veloxa from two kinds of source, released over the first week: call transcripts and system exports. When they disagree, it's your job to work out which to believe.
Transcripts are machine-generated: names, tools and numbers may be misheard, and speakers may be wrong or biased. The exports are better but have quirks of their own. Some things that look like mistakes aren't. Nobody will confirm which is which.
Rules of engagement
AI is allowed, and expected. Use any assistant you like. You will be judged on the decisions you make with it and on explaining your system without it.
Requirements arrive over time. New transcripts and voice notes add, change and contradict what you know. Plan for change, not a frozen spec.
Live sessions. Reviews on days 2, 4 and 8 (show what runs; expect to make a change live and explain it). On day 6, a 30-minute whiteboard session with no screen: draw your data model and walk through three conflicts you resolved. On day 10, a 60-minute final.
ASSUMPTIONS.md. Date, what you assumed, the source line it rests on, confidence, what would change your mind. Update entries when they're proved wrong; don't delete them.
TRANSCRIPT_NOTES.md. Everything you think was misheard or contradicts another source, the evidence you used, and what you concluded.
DECISIONS.md. Choices you could defend either way: data model, storage, agent memory, what the cockpit refuses to answer.
Commit daily with messages a teammate could follow. We read the history. Code freezes at the end of day 9.
Scope
Must have
The data room loaded into a data model you design, reconciled with the transcripts.
The 14 people as AI agents you can interview, grounded in the data. Where the data is silent (their lives, their private thoughts), invent it and log it as an assumption.
A cockpit where the CEO asks one question and gets a short answer that cites the records behind it, plus a "what should I worry about" view.
A response to every CEO voice note as it arrives: a change, or a written pushback.
Stretch
Agents that keep living after 31 Oct 2026 and generate new activity day by day.
"What did we know on date X?" questions.
An automated test set for the cockpit's answers.
What we look at
Working code matters, but judgement matters more. In rough order of weight:
The live sessions: can you explain and change your own system without help?
Whether the cockpit's answers are true against the data room, cite their sources, and admit what they don't know.
How you read the sources: what you trusted, what you doubted, and the evidence for each.
Your logs, especially entries you revised.
How you handled change, including requests you pushed back on.
Whether the 14 people feel real, and the code: readable, one-command setup.
There is no single right solution. Doing the must-haves well beats doing everything badly.
You get | You don't get
A data room of exports from Veloxa's systems, in three drops (days 1, 3 and 4) | A schema, a data dictionary, or a list of which export is right
Auto-generated summaries of leadership calls and CEO voice notes, released on days we choose | Live time with the CEO or leadership, or corrections when a transcript is wrong
Three 30-minute reviews, one whiteboard session and a final session with a reviewer (not a stakeholder; won't answer business questions) | The questions the CEO will ask in the final
Any AI tools you like | A tech stack
